meta.landingTitle: Read & write any form, in any language.
meta.landingDesc: PolyglotFormFill reads a form in one language and fills it from your data in another — on your device, privately. We never see your data.
hero.lede: Reads a form in one language, fills it from your data in another — PDFs, Word, Excel and web forms. All on your device; nothing is uploaded, ever.
hero.trust: AES-256 vault · passkey unlock · no cloud · no tracking · open & auditable
flow.deviceTitle: On your device — where all the processing happens
flow.egressLabel: What leaves — only what you send, to whom you send it:
flow.egressBody: a form you submit goes straight to the recipient you picked · a web search you type sends only those words. Nothing passes through us — no documents, no vault, no identifiers.
feat.h2: Turn a non-fillable PDF into a form you can actually fill
feat.sub: A flat PDF with no form fields — even a photo or a scan — becomes a real, fillable form in seconds. No printing, no re-scanning, no uploading it to a website.
feat.mainTitle: Any flat PDF, scan, or photo becomes an editable form
feat.mainBody: On-device OCR reads the layout, works out where every field belongs, places real form fields there and fills them from your vault. Then export a clean, filled PDF.
feat.c1b: OCR, translation, filling and signing run locally. Your data never travels to us or anyone.
feat.c2b: Fill a form in any language from your data in any other — a Japanese form from Hindi details, or the other way round. Translation runs on your device.
feat.c3b: Fills .docx and .xlsx forms — named fields or flat labels — and can export a PDF.
feat.c4b: Answer a new field once; it's remembered — encrypted, on your device — for next time.
feat.c5b: Non-delegable, device-bound signatures with verifiable provenance. Nobody signs on your behalf.
feat.c6b: Your passphrase stays on your device. It is checked there, on your own machine, to unlock your vault — it is never sent anywhere and never stored, by us or by anyone else. Prefer hardware? Unlock with a passkey (WebAuthn) instead.
feat.c7b: The extension fills web forms; the desktop app holds your keys as a hardened trust anchor.
who.h2: Built for anyone who fills forms across languages and borders
who.sub: Three groups get the most out of it — and every one keeps their data on their own device.
who.c1b: Turn scanned visa, residency and settlement PDFs into fillable forms, and complete them in a client's language — without a document ever leaving your machine.
who.c2b: Tax, banking and onboarding forms rarely arrive in your language. Fill them from your own details, held in an encrypted vault on your device, and export a clean PDF.
who.c3b: Every step runs locally with zero telemetry, and the vault unlocks with a passphrase or hardware passkey. No account, no cloud, no tracking.
band.h2: Your data in your language. The form in theirs.
band.sub: Governments and institutions publish forms in one language; people hold their details in another. PolyglotFormFill closes that gap on-device — it reads and fills forms in any language, and translates between roughly 200 languages, any to any.
price.h2: Buy once. Own it. No subscription.
price.sub: Try everything free for 7 days. Then one payment, per device, verified offline — no subscription, no account, no activation server.
price.freeList: Then a one-time purchase to keep it

get.note: The Windows installer is code-signed (verified publisher: Subramanya Mysore); a new signed app can still show a SmartScreen notice — click More info, then Run anyway. The extension installs with no prompt. macOS & Linux next.

install.title: Install PolyglotFormFill
install.intro: Start with the browser extension — it’s the fastest way in and does the core job. The desktop app adds signing, history and offline work.
install.extLoad: Until it’s on the stores, load it in developer mode:
install.extStep1: Unzip the download to a folder.
install.extStep4: Click Load unpacked → select the unzipped folder. PolyglotFormFill now appears in your extensions list.
install.extStep5: Pin it to the toolbar so you can find it: click the puzzle-piece icon 🧩 near the top-right of the browser (that’s the Extensions menu), find PolyglotFormFill, and click the pin 📌 next to it. Its icon now sits on your toolbar.
install.extStep6: Click that PolyglotFormFill toolbar icon → set a passphrase (or unlock with a passkey).
install.extStep7: Under “Your details” in the popup, type each field (e.g. full_name, email, phone) and its value, then Save field. These are stored encrypted on your device. Then open a form and click Fill this page.
install.extNote: Don’t see a toolbar icon right after loading? That’s normal — Chrome hides new extensions behind the 🧩 puzzle-piece menu until you pin them (step 5). Firefox: use about:debugging → “Load Temporary Add-on”, then pin from the toolbar overflow.
install.wingetBody: Windows has a built-in package manager. Once our listing is approved, the desktop app installs with one command — no download prompt, and no warning to click through:
install.wingetNote: winget fetches the installer and checks it against a published checksum before running it. Not live yet — the listing is awaiting review in the Windows Package Manager repository. Until then, use the direct download below.
install.headsTitle: What Windows will show you, and why.
install.headsBody: We haven’t bought a code-signing certificate yet — they’re sold to registered companies and cost a few hundred dollars a year, and we’d rather put that off than charge you for it. Windows therefore doesn’t recognise the publisher name yet, and shows this blue box the first time you run the installer:
install.screenBody: Microsoft Defender SmartScreen prevented an unrecognised app from starting.
install.headsMeans: That message means “I haven’t seen this publisher before” — not that anything is wrong with the file. To continue:
install.headsStep1: Click More info (small link inside the blue box).
install.headsAfter: It appears once, on first install. Prefer to avoid it entirely? Use winget above, or the browser extension, which is unaffected.
install.signedBody: Code-signed by a Microsoft-trusted certificate authority, so Windows shows the verified publisher — Subramanya Mysore — not “unknown publisher.”
install.deskNote: On first launch you’ll set a passphrase — the app is locked until you enter it.
install.verifySummary: Check the download is exactly what we published
install.verifyBody: Every release lists the SHA-256 of each file. Run this in PowerShell on the file you downloaded and compare — if the two strings match, the file arrived intact and unaltered.

privP.title: Privacy Policy
privP.authNote: This translation is provided for your convenience. The English version of this Privacy Policy is the authoritative and legally binding version.
privP.disclaimer: ⚖ Draft pending legal review — not legal advice. This is a drafting template for the PolyglotFormFill product. It must be reviewed and approved by qualified legal counsel in each jurisdiction where the Service is offered (incl. the EU/EEA under the GDPR, India under the DPDP Act 2023, and the US under the CCPA/CPRA) before publication. Contact/identity fields are completed; a final read by counsel is still recommended before wide public release.
privP.tldr: The substance, plainly: We do not see, store, or transmit your documents or the data you enter, and we do not send them anywhere you did not intend. Everything is processed on your device. Your content leaves your device only when you take a specific action — submitting a completed form to the recipient you choose, or a web search you type — and it goes directly there, never through us.
privP.b1: This Policy is issued by Subramanya Mysore (sole proprietor), India ("we", "us"), responsible for the PolyglotFormFill application, browser extension, and website (the "Service"). For the GDPR we act as data controller; under the India DPDP Act 2023 as the Data Fiduciary; where we process no personal data, no such role arises. Grievance Officer / Contact: Subramanya Mysore · subumysore@gmail.com.
privP.def1: Personal Data — information relating to an identifiable natural person.
privP.def2: User Content — the documents, forms, images, and values you enter or store (your "vault"), including any Personal Data within them.
privP.def3: Device — the computer or device on which you run the Service.
privP.b3: The Service is designed so that we do not see, store, or transmit your User Content, and we do not send it to any location you did not intend. Specifically:
privP.p3a: On-device processing. Reading/rendering, OCR, translation, field detection, filling, export, and signing are performed locally on your Device. We do not receive your User Content to do them.
privP.p3b: No collection by us. We do not collect, receive, access, or store your User Content. There is no account required and no upload of your User Content to us.
privP.p3c: User-directed transmission only. User Content leaves your Device only when you initiate a specific action, and only to the destination you choose:
privP.egressA: (a) Submitting a completed form — transmitted directly from your Device to the recipient you select (e.g. a government or vendor site). We do not proxy, intercept, receive, retain, or access it.
privP.egressB: (b) Web search (optional) — only the search terms you type are sent, directly to the third-party search provider (DuckDuckGo), to return results. No User Content, vault data, or identifiers are sent. Enter a URL to avoid this entirely.
privP.p3end: These are the only circumstances in which content or search terms leave your Device — each user-initiated, clearly labelled, and directed to a destination you selected.
privP.h4: Limited non-content data we may process
privP.li4a: Software distribution & updates. Downloading/updating the Service, or its download of assets (updates, fonts, models), makes a one-way request to the relevant channel, which may process technical data (e.g. IP) as an independent controller under its own policy. This is a download to your Device and provides no path to upload your User Content.
privP.li4b: Payments & licensing. Paid features are unlocked by an offline signed license verified on your Device (contacts no server). If you purchase, payment is handled by not applicable (no paid features yet); we receive only what is needed to issue/support the license (e.g. name, email, order id) — never your User Content.
privP.li4c: Voluntary communications. If you contact support, we process what you provide to respond.
privP.b4end: We do not use analytics, advertising identifiers, tracking technologies, or content-bearing crash reporting.
privP.b5: For the limited processing in §4: contract (Art. 6(1)(b)) for licensing/support; legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f)) for secure distribution/updates; consent (Art. 6(1)(a)) where required. No legal basis is required for User Content because we do not process it.
privP.li6a: Your vault is stored only on your Device and is encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM).
privP.li6b: The key is derived on unlock from your passphrase or a hardware passkey (WebAuthn); it is never stored and never transmitted.
privP.li6c: The extension uses least-privilege permissions and contains no remote code (Manifest V3).
privP.b7: Because we do not receive your User Content, we do not share, sell, or transfer it. For the limited non-content data in §4, we share only with the providers named there, under contract; any cross-border transfer follows that provider's safeguards.
privP.b8: We do not retain your User Content (we never receive it). Non-content data in §4 is retained only as long as necessary.
privP.b9: Subject to applicable law (GDPR Arts. 15–22; India DPDP Ch. III; CCPA/CPRA) you may have rights to access, correct, delete, port, restrict, or object, to withdraw consent, and to complain to a supervisory authority / the Data Protection Board. Because your User Content resides solely on your Device, you access and delete it directly (in the Service or by removing local data). For the limited non-content data we hold, contact subumysore@gmail.com.
privP.b10: The Service is not directed to, and we do not knowingly process Personal Data of, children under 13.
privP.b11: We may update this Policy; material changes update the Effective date and, where required, include additional notice.
privP.footer: Subramanya Mysore (sole proprietor) · Grievance Officer/Contact: Subramanya Mysore · subumysore@gmail.com · DPO/EU Representative if appointed. PolyglotFormFill — privacy-first, on-device form autofill.

get.extPrimary: Get the browser extension — no warnings
install.androidH2: On an Android phone or tablet
install.androidIntro: The autofill add-on runs on Android inside a Chromium browser that supports extensions — Kiwi Browser is the easiest. (Chrome for Android does not support extensions.)
install.androidStep1: Install Kiwi Browser from Google Play (it is Chromium-based and supports Chrome extensions).
install.androidStep2: Download the extension file below to your phone.
install.androidStep3: In Kiwi, open the ⋮ menu → Extensions, turn on Developer mode, then tap “+ (from .zip/.crx/.user.js)” and choose the file you just downloaded.
install.androidStep4: Open ⋮ → Extensions → PolyglotFormFill, unlock your vault, and fill forms in the mobile browser.
install.androidStoreNote: Or open our Chrome Web Store listing in Kiwi and tap “Add to Kiwi”.
install.androidDeskNote: The full desktop app is for Windows PCs and laptops — it does not run on Android. Use a Windows laptop for the desktop app; a native mobile app is on our roadmap.
